_schema: fish_id -> { name, rod, net, deep:true (deep-drop RIG pool ONLY — bait-gated, never rolls on the surface rod/net), w:{dawn,day,dusk,night}, WEATHER IN THREE TIERS (calm / rain / storm, mutually exclusive — see FishTable.RAIN_MIN): storm: ok|only|never|bonus for a full squall, rain: ok|only|never|bonus for the drizzle either side of one, fog: ok|only|never|bonus for the sea-fog bank a squall leaves behind, light: any|drawn (comes UP to lit water after dark)|shy (will not come up while the floodlights burn, hour irrelevant — kill the breaker to fish it), water: any|near|open (open = >10 m off the rig rim; on the DEEP rig that is a function of DROP HEIGHT, since the lead's throw is fixed and only a fall from the topside plate or higher carries it clear), depth: surface|mid|deep (the band the visible school swims in), drop_m (DEEP POOL ONLY: metres the deep rig's lead must sink before this species will take the bait — the ladder that makes a long drop fish deeper; past it the species thins out by FishTable.DROP_FADE_PER_M), bait:{item_id: multiplier} this species' OWN opinion of what is on the hook, on top of the general deep/shallow/rate profile in FishTable.BAIT_TABLE (deep pool only — the surface rod and the net fish bare), size_kg:[min,max] landed weight rolled per catch, fillets:[min,max] portions ONE fish gives the stove or the drying line, scaled across its own size_kg (a species with fillets is a 'big' fish: it also cures straight from raw on a drying line instead of turning), fight, pull, cooked_to, school:{count,size,tint:[r,g,b],active:phases}, note }. One source of truth: rod rolls, net rolls, deep-drop rolls, stove map, visible schools, and the Fisherman's Handbook readable are ALL generated from this table.

fish_copper_sprat.name: Copper Sprat
fish_copper_sprat.note: Bait-tier shoals that trail anything moving. The sea's small change.

fish_herring.name: Lantern Herring
fish_herring.note: The gateway catch. At night the shoal glows its own position away.

fish_slate_cod.name: Slate Cod
fish_slate_cod.note: Loves a gray sky — bites double under storm cloud. Heavy, honest meat.

fish_mirrorjack.name: Mirrorjack
fish_mirrorjack.note: A dawn and dusk feeder in open water — fast, chrome, furious on the line.

fish_chimefish.name: Chimefish
fish_chimefish.note: Calm seas only — they won't ring in weather. Worth more traded than eaten, someday.

fish_silver_ladder.name: Silver Ladder
fish_silver_ladder.note: Dawn columns over open water — the shoal stacks vertical, a shimmering pillar.

fish_ember_snapper.name: Ember Snapper
fish_ember_snapper.note: Warm-bodied — crowds the rig's outfalls and warm steel. Fish the shadow of the deck.

fish_sable_hake.name: Sable Hake
fish_sable_hake.note: Rises to worklight after dark like moths with fins. Power the floodlights and fish the glow.

fish_ghost_sole.name: Ghost Sole
fish_ghost_sole.note: Near-invisible by day. Night water near a glow is where it shows itself.

fish_glasspike.name: Glasspike
fish_glasspike.note: Clear still nights, open water — a pike you see through, found by the grit in its gut.

fish_lodestone_bream.name: Lodestone Bream
fish_lodestone_bream.note: Deep daylight water. Its magnetized bones spin a compass — catch enough, craft crude magnets, someday.

fish_drum_croaker.name: Drum Croaker
fish_drum_croaker.note: Storm fish, full stop. You hear the chorus drumming through the hull as the rain comes — then they bite like they mean it.

fish_inkwell_squid.name: Inkwell Squid
fish_inkwell_squid.note: Night jigging. Comes up backwards in a huff of luminous ink — the ink's worth keeping too, someday.

fish_ribbon_eel.name: Ribbon Eel
fish_ribbon_eel.note: The first thing the deep rig reaches — 8 m down is enough. Dark water only. Comes up faintly crackling; the Bloom keeps strange batteries.

fish_barrel_grouper.name: Goliath Grouper
fish_barrel_grouper.note: Rarest thing the spool reaches and the whole reason for the deep rig: 26 m of open water before one will look at a bait, and nothing under thirty kilos comes up. A storm stirs them up off the bottom. One fish breaks down into six to twelve fillets, by its size — a big one feeds you for a week. Never on the surface rod: this is a deep-rig fish and only a deep-rig fish.

fish_stone_crab.name: Stone Crab
fish_stone_crab.note: Walks into a soaked net, never onto a hook. Shell's ceramic-hard — keep the pieces, someday.

fish_gutter_prawn.name: Gutter Prawn
fish_gutter_prawn.note: Net filler. A soak rarely comes up without a few — the pens will want them, someday.

fish_miller_flounder.name: Miller's Flounder
fish_miller_flounder.note: Deck-plate camouflage, bottom habits. Nets working close to the legs find them by day.

fish_fathom_halibut.name: Fathom Halibut
fish_fathom_halibut.note: Door-sized. Only a night-soaked net brings one up, and the winch knows about it. Breaks down into one to three fillets — careful with that filet.

the_looker.name: The Looker
the_looker.note: Any water, any hour, almost never. It is not kept. You'll understand at the rail.

fish_gulper_eel.name: Gulper Eel
fish_gulper_eel.note: Deep-drop rig only, and not until the lead is 34 m down. All jaw and gut — it swallows things bigger than itself. Night water, off the bottom, on a baited hook.

fish_bloom_dragon.name: Bloom Dragonfish
fish_bloom_dragon.note: Deep-drop rig only, 38 m down in the black. Its own lure burns blue-green down there. Rises harder to a baited hook when the worklights are on.

fish_fathom_sturgeon.name: Fathom Sturgeon
fish_fathom_sturgeon.note: Deep-drop rig only, and the deepest thing the spool reaches — 44 m, the end of the line. Armoured, ancient, patient: the longest fight in the sea. A storm stirs them up off the bottom, and one breaks down into five to nine prime fillets.

fish_abyss_grenadier.name: Abyss Grenadier
fish_abyss_grenadier.note: Deep-drop rig only, from 24 m down. A rattail that hangs nose-down over the deep in daylight; open water, dropped straight below. Three to six prime fillets off one.

fish_bilge_blenny.name: Bilge Blenny
fish_bilge_blenny.note: Lives in the wash around the legs and the outfalls, and never once leaves the rig's shadow. Ugly, endless, and always biting.

fish_tallow_pollock.name: Tallow Pollock
fish_tallow_pollock.note: Fat under the skin like a candle — bites double with weather in the water, and renders down to a proper meal.

fish_gannet_mackerel.name: Gannet Mackerel
fish_gannet_mackerel.note: Runs the open water at first and last light and scatters the moment the glass falls. Where the birds are working, they are.

fish_rust_wrasse.name: Rust Wrasse
fish_rust_wrasse.note: Grazes the barnacle crust off the legs all day long and comes up the colour of the steel it eats. Fish the shadow.

fish_kelp_pipefish.name: Kelp Pipefish
fish_kelp_pipefish.note: Hangs vertical in the bloom-kelp and holds dead still. Never takes a hook; walks into a soaked net without noticing it.

fish_lantern_dogfish.name: Lantern Dogfish
fish_lantern_dogfish.note: A small shark with a lit belly, and it fights like a bigger one. Deep open water, and only well after dark.

fish_squall_garfish.name: Squall Garfish
fish_squall_garfish.note: Storm water only, and only out where the swell has room. Comes clean out of the sea on the strike and goes back in somewhere else entirely.

fish_anchor_ray.name: Anchor Ray
fish_anchor_ray.note: Lies on the mooring chains where the silt collects. Only a net soaked close to the legs finds one, and the winch complains about it.

fish_trench_hagfish.name: Trench Hagfish
fish_trench_hagfish.note: Deep-drop rig only, from 28 m down. Comes up in a rope of its own slime and keeps moving after it should have stopped. Sears to a prime fillet regardless.

fish_coelacanth.name: Coelacanth
fish_coelacanth.note: Deep-drop rig only, from 20 m down. A rare catch from the deep — armoured, alien, and worth keeping. Four fillets of fine, oily meat.

fish_swordfish.name: Swordfish
fish_swordfish.note: Deep-drop rig only, from 22 m down, and it comes up in the RAIN. Open water off a high drop, on a whole baitfish — a chunk of shell or a snail is beneath its notice. It hunts the falling glass: put a herring on the hook the hour the weather comes in and hold the drum at twenty-two. All bill and shoulder, the longest run on the line, and six to thirteen prime fillets off one.

fish_skipjack_tuna.name: Skipjack Tuna
fish_skipjack_tuna.note: The small one, and never alone — skipjack boil the surface in open water by day.

fish_yellowfin_tuna.name: Yellowfin Tuna
fish_yellowfin_tuna.note: Gold down the flank and sickle fins half its own length. Runs when it feels the hook.

fish_albacore_tuna.name: Albacore Tuna
fish_albacore_tuna.note: Pectorals like scythes, reaching most of the way down it. Cold water, long runs.

fish_bigeye_tuna.name: Bigeye Tuna
fish_bigeye_tuna.note: That eye is for the dark water it hunts in. Comes up at dusk, goes down by morning.

fish_bluefin_tuna.name: Bluefin Tuna
fish_bluefin_tuna.note: The big one. A quarter tonne of muscle built like a torpedo — it will empty the spool.

fish_bluelined_grouper.name: Bluelined Grouper
fish_bluelined_grouper.note: Electric blue pinstripes on olive. Holds station in the leg shadow and waits.

fish_peacock_grouper.name: Peacock Grouper
fish_peacock_grouper.note: Covered in blue eyespots, every one ringed black. It watches the whole reef at once.

fish_humpback_grouper.name: Humpback Grouper
fish_humpback_grouper.note: Small head on a steep white back, all over black spots. Odd, slow, unbothered.

fish_leopard_grouper.name: Leopard Coral Grouper
fish_leopard_grouper.note: Coral red, spotted electric blue, and faster off the mark than a fish that size has any right to be.

fish_mahi_mahi.name: Mahi-Mahi
fish_mahi_mahi.note: Green-gold and lit from inside, with a forehead like a blunt axe. Fast, and it jumps.

fish_swallowtail.name: Swallowtail Angelfish
fish_swallowtail.note: Two long tail filaments trailing behind it like a swallow. Barely worth eating; worth looking at.
